subject: Forecast-driven reserve allocation & price contingency request
messages:
From: Ben Walsh <ben.walsh@astrahealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Astra Health Procurement <procurement@astrahealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Forecast-driven reserve ask & pricing guardrails

Vivek —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran a deeper forecast with our ML team and are looking at a committed plan that ramps across the next 12 months as we roll LLM features into our clinician workflows. Two things we need to lock down before we can finalize the SOW:

1) Pricing protection: the GPU market is volatile and we need a clear guardrail if underlying GPU costs spike. Can Redwood provide a trigger-based adjustment or a capped surcharge mechanism tied to an industry GPU index?

2) Capacity sizing that maps to our forecasted token mix: our peak window is short but intense (inference-heavy, long-context retrieval). We want to avoid paying for permanently reserved capacity we won’t use while ensuring headroom for burst windows.

Attached is a simple forecast (CSV + notes) — happy to walk through. Next step for us is procurement sign-off, but we need a term construct (tenor + discount gating) that our finance team can take to legal.

Best,
Ben
Ben Walsh
Head of Platform & Data
Astra Health
[Attachment: astra_forecast_q3_q4.csv (CSV)]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Ben Walsh <ben.walsh@astrahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T12:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Forecast-driven reserve ask & pricing guardrails

Ben — thanks for the clear ask and the forecast. I reviewed the token mix briefly; we should be able to build a reserve structure that ties committed units to your rolling 3-month forecast while adding a small buffer for burst windows. Two pragmatic constructs we recommend:

- Forecast-driven phasing: commit levels that step up monthly (or quarterly) tied to your submitted forecast; unused committed units can be rolled forward for 3 months (credit buffer) so you don’t pay for permanent slack.
- Price contingency: implement a two-part guardrail — (A) a trigger that pauses new discount tranches if the GPU index (we reference BGPU-Spot-Index) increases >20% over a 30-day rolling average, and (B) a capped surcharge that only applies if wholesale costs exceed a preset threshold; surcharge capped at X% and only for the months where the trigger fires.

I attached a capacity model (capacity_model_v3.xlsx) with example phasing and three sensitivity scenarios (base / +25% GPU cost / +50% GPU cost). Karthik and Marissa — please see the sensitivity table (Tab "Pricing Sigs") and advise on approval gates we need for a 12-month vs 6-month tenor.

Ben — if this looks directionally right I’ll formalize language for procurement and attach a redlined term summary.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: capacity_model_v3.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Walsh <ben.walsh@astrahealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-24T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Forecast-driven reserve ask & pricing guardrails

Agree with Vivek's construct. A few practical asks from the sales/ops side:

- We should offer a phased discount schedule: 0–3 months (onboarding) = minimal discount, 4–6 months = mid discount, 7–12 months = full committed discount. That reduces our exposure while giving the customer runway.
- For the GPU-index trigger, legal will want an objective published source (BGPU-Spot-Index link) + a clear calculation example in the SOW.
- Need finance / legal sign-off for any surcharge cap >10% — Marissa, can you run the scenario P&L for a 12-month commit with surcharge caps at 10% vs 20%?

Ben — I’ll own sequencing with procurement. Vivek — if you send the draft summary I’ll add the commercial milestones and HubSpot stage changes. Linking the HS entry here: https://hubspot.com/deals/ASTRA-2026-09

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Director, Sales Ops
[No attachments]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Walsh <ben.walsh@astrahealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-26T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Forecast-driven reserve ask & pricing guardrails

High level financials attached (redwood_reserve_term_summary.pdf). Key takeaways from the three scenarios I ran:

- Base case: 12-month commit @ 15% discount - IRR on GPU capacity healthy, unit economics protected.
- +25% GPU cost scenario: with a surcharge cap at 10% we remain slightly profitable; with 20% cap margins get thin but acceptable for strategic accounts.
- +50% GPU cost scenario: surcharge above 20% required to keep go-forward cost-neutral — this is high risk for us.

Recommendation: approve a 12-month tenor with tiered discounting (full discount begins in month 7) and a price-contingency clause: surcharge allowed only if BGPU-Spot-Index > baseline by 30% for a sustained 30 days; surcharge cap = 15% for executive-approved strategic deals. Also include a credit-buffer mechanic: unused committed tokens roll forward for up to 3 months.

I've attached a one-pager with the proposed gating language and the scenario table. If legal wants different thresholds we can adjust but ask that leadership sign off on the 15% cap for this strategic pilot.

Marissa
VP, Finance — Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_reserve_term_summary.pdf (PDF)]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-09-01T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Exec approval request: Astra 12mo commit with 15% surcharge cap

Monica —

Requesting exec exception to authorize the following for Astra Health (deal ASTRA-2026-09):

- Tenor: 12 months; phased discounts with full committed discount effective month 7.
- Price contingency: BGPU-Spot-Index trigger = baseline +30% sustained for 30 days. If triggered, a surcharge may be applied but capped at 15% (executive exception).
- Credit buffer: unused committed units roll forward for up to 3 months.
- Attach docs: redwood_reserve_term_summary.pdf and the draft MA with the above clause (signed-ma-proposal-draft.docx).

Ben is in procurement and ready to move if we sign off. Marissa's scenario table is attached and shows acceptable P&L at 15% cap in our +25% case. Karthik — we’ll rely on you to map milestones.

If ok, please reply with any changes; otherwise I’ll mark HubSpot as "Contracting - Awaiting Signature" and push to legal.

Thanks,
Vivek
[Attachment: signed-ma-proposal-draft.docx (DOCX)]
